correctness.rationale: The exact QP correction is the Euclidean projection of u=(0,-1) onto the active linearized disk half-space. Writing s as the squared half-step norm and d as the squared distance to u gives lambda=1-d/(2s) and the corrected full step x-plus=c h with c=1-eta+eta d/(2s). The submitted polynomial bound proves the full step is strictly inside the disk, while direct expansion proves the next half-step is strictly outside, so induction gives persistent alternation. The exact ratio formula for d_{t+1}/d_t and the uniform bound on its bracket yield the stated contraction rho(eta)<1; geometric decay then gives both pointwise limits and O(1/T) convergence of the averaged half-step to the boundary point. The inspected rational-arithmetic checker is consistent with representative trajectories, and an independent numerical replay across several eta values reproduced the outside/inside alternation and contraction.

value.rationale: The result resolves the behavior of the canonical curved-constraint witness used to motivate an averaged-feasibility obstruction: every sampled half-step remains infeasible, yet averaging removes the violation at an explicit O(1/T) rate. That distinction directly limits what this witness can prove about asymptotic averaged infeasibility and supplies a reusable exact trajectory benchmark for primal-QP extragradient methods.
